steps.title: Say goodbye nicely
steps.prompt:
DELETE removes rows - like crossing a name off a guest list.
Always use WHERE, so only the intended row goes.
steps.task: Try typing: DELETE FROM customers WHERE name = 'Khadija Sabri';
hints: Name the customer you want to remove.
Use WHERE with the name in quotes.
Write: DELETE FROM customers WHERE name = 'Khadija Sabri';
steps.expected_sql: DELETE FROM customers WHERE name = 'Khadija Sabri';
steps.memory_trick: DELETE FROM + WHERE = 'remove exactly these rows'.

steps.title: Delete by id
steps.prompt:
Rows are safer to delete by their ID - it's unique. Fill the blank:
DELETE FROM customers WHERE id = ___;
hints: We delete the one with id 12.

steps.title: Predict the scariest DELETE
steps.prompt:
What does this do?
DELETE FROM products;
hints: An unfiltered DELETE clears the whole table.
steps.memory_trick: DELETE without WHERE = the whole table. You'll be warned first.

steps.title: Why the warning?
steps.prompt:
Real databases can't be Reset. In a real shop, DELETE FROM products; would empty the shelves for good.
That's why the app gently warns you - and why you practice so a real DELETE never surprises you.
steps.task: In a REAL (non-practice) database, what happens to DELETEd rows?
hints: There's no Reset button in real life.
Think of a paper register being cut up.
The rows are removed from the table.
